title: On the Monitorability of Natural Language Autoencoders: Identification vs Discrimination
abstract: arXiv:2610.18727v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Natural Language Autoencoders (NLAs) are proposed as oversight tools for language models: an Activation Verbaliser (AV) writes an English explanation of an activation vector, and an Activation Reconstructor (AR) maps the explanation back to a vector. Their value for oversight depends on a human monitor being able to tell a true account of an activation from a false one, given the AV's explanation. We formalise NLA training and NLA oversight deployment as two different referential games from Emergent Communication: training is a generative referential game, while oversight is a discriminative, multi-modal, partially-observable referential game played over a many-to-many relation between the monitored language model's activations and the accounts that are true of them. translated_title: 论自然语言自编码器的可监控性：识别与判别
translated_abstract: 自然语言自编码器（NLA）被提出作为语言模型的监督工具：激活言语化器（AV）为激活向量撰写英文解释，而激活重构器（AR）将解释映射回向量。它们在监督中的价值取决于人类监控者在给定AV解释的情况下，能否将一段对激活的真实叙述与虚假叙述区分开来。我们将NLA的训练与NLA监督部署形式化为源自涌现通信领域的两种不同的指称博弈：训练是一种生成式指称博弈，而监督是一种判别式的、多模态的、部分可观测的指称博弈，该博弈在受监控语言模型的激活与真实描述它们的叙述之间的多对多关系上展开。这两种博弈之间的差距预示着AV的解释将能够识别其所描述的是哪个激活，却无法将其真实叙述与紧密匹配的叙述区分开来。
tldr: 论文将自然语言自编码器的训练与监督部署形式化为两种不同的指称博弈，并指出二者之间的差距导致其解释虽能识别对应的激活，却难以让人类监控者从多个近似叙述中辨别出真实的那一个。
en_tdlr: The paper formalizes NLA training and oversight as two distinct referential games and shows that the gap between them means AV explanations can identify which activation they describe but fail to help human monitors discriminate true accounts from closely matching false ones.
